hero.heading: Drag'n Wash Beginner Guide
hero.lead: Start with a careful wash pass, listen for comfort prompts, and keep a clean save before late branches. This Drag'n Wash beginner guide focuses on progress habits that prevent stuck jobs and wasted replays.

sections.heading: What You Do in the First Session
sections.intro: The opening hour teaches the same loop you will use for every ending.
paragraphs: Drag'n Wash puts you in charge of a soap-and-wash service for dragons. Your job is to clean thoroughly, keep conversation going, and respond when comfort unlocks personal requests. Official materials describe a simulation pace rather than combat or inventory crafting, so attention and camera angles matter more than memorized hotkey charts.

Expect a single-player session measured in tens of minutes, not multi-day grinds. Official copy places each ending near ninety minutes. That means early mistakes—missed dirt, ignored prompts, or overwriting the only save—are expensive. Treat your first clear as practice for route planning later.

The game is adult-only. Comfort growth can unlock mature romance and personal scenes. This page explains how to progress those systems at a high level without explicit detail. If a prompt feels out of order, pause and finish the wash or request the visit is currently highlighting.

sections.heading: First Wash Steps
sections.intro: A practical order of operations for your opening visits.

steps.heading: Confirm platform and input
steps.description: Launch from Steam or itch on Windows, macOS, or Linux (Steam Deck Verified per official Sep 15, 2026 Steam news). Full controller support is listed on Steam—if you prefer a pad, connect it before the first wash and open Options for Invert Look Y or Sprayer Reduce Motion from the Kobold Hotfix if camera or sprayer motion feels off.

steps.heading: Do a slow full-body pass
steps.description: Clean obvious surfaces first, then deliberately check tails, neck backs, and other easy-to-miss angles. Itch comments say the clean bar can look full while a job still refuses to finish because of leftover dirt or ink in those spots.

steps.heading: Follow chat and comfort prompts
steps.description: Talk as you wash. When the visit surfaces a personal request, complete it in the prompted order. Out-of-order personal request handling is a community-reported softlock risk on later Conrad visits.

steps.heading: Save before late branches
steps.description: When a visit feels like it is approaching a major beat or credits, duplicate or keep a separate slot. Continuing after finishing a slot can dump you into credits, which wastes route options.

sections.heading: Stuck Clean Bar Checklist
sections.intro: When the meter looks done but the job will not complete.
paragraphs: This is the most common early frustration in itch comments. The UI can read as nearly complete while a tiny missed patch blocks the finish state. Assume you missed geometry before assuming a broken meter.

subsections.heading: Restart the job and re-scout
paragraphs: Back out or restart the wash job if the game allows, then re-enter with a scavenger mindset. Circle the dragon slowly. Prioritize the tail, the back of the neck, and any inked or patterned areas that blend into wet shading.
bullets: Check ink on the tail
Check the back of the neck
Change camera height and orbit both sides
Finish remaining soap or tool passes before forcing dialogue

subsections.heading: If it still will not finish
paragraphs: Reload an earlier save and repeat the pass with a different camera distance. Confirm you are not mid-request with an unresolved prompt. Softlock-like states are more often tied to request order or credits interactions than to the clean bar alone. For a fuller recovery path, use the escape guide.

sections.heading: Comfort, Chat, and Personal Requests
paragraphs: Comfort is the pacing layer on top of cleaning. Washing well keeps the visit moving; chat and attentive responses raise comfort so new requests appear. Official framing is “tend to requests as comfort grows,” not a published percentage table. React to what the current visit shows on screen.

When a request appears, treat it as part of the critical path for that visit. Itch comments warn that completing personal requests out of the prompted order can softlock later Conrad content. Keep the tone practical: finish the highlighted ask, then return to any remaining wash work.
Adult scenes exist deeper in comfort growth. Consistent cleaning, attentive dialogue, and ordered requests are enough for a first clear without memorizing fragile dialogue trees.

links.label: Plan endings after your first clear

sections.heading: Save Tips Before You Chase Endings
paragraphs: Official structure is three endings at roughly ninety minutes each. That is short enough to replay, but long enough that careless overwrites hurt. Keep a “safe hub” save before late branches, and a separate slot per route you intend to finish.

After a slot reaches credits, continuing from that same file can drop you back into credits instead of a flexible free-play state. Players also report a softlock risk if you select unstuck kobold during credits—avoid experimental menu choices there even though the official Kobold Hotfix added Unstick Kobold on the pause menu for stuck play states.

A simple Drag'n Wash beginner routine is enough: one careful wash, one backup save, and no experiments in the credits menu. Once that feels automatic, the endings and escape pages become useful instead of overwhelming.

faq.question: How long is a beginner clear?
faq.answer: Official materials describe about ninety minutes per ending. Your first session may run longer while you learn camera angles and request pacing.

faq.question: Why won’t my wash job finish?
faq.answer: Itch comments usually point to missed dirt—especially ink on the tail or the back of the neck—even when the clean bar looks full. Restart the job and recheck hard-to-see spots.

faq.question: Do I need exact trust percentages?
faq.answer: No. Official Drag'n Wash progression is framed around washing, chatting, and tending requests as comfort grows. Follow on-screen prompts.

faq.question: Should I use a controller?
faq.answer: You can. Steam lists full controller support for Drag'n Wash. Check Options for Invert Look Y and Sprayer Reduce Motion from the official Kobold Hotfix.

faq.question: When should I read the endings guide?
faq.answer: After one comfortable Drag'n Wash wash loop, or immediately if you already know you want multiple endings and need save-slot strategy.

hero.heading: Drag'n Wash Endings Guide
hero.lead: Official materials confirm three endings at about ninety minutes each. This Drag'n Wash endings guide explains how to plan routes and saves with Official versus Community labels kept clear.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: Three Endings
sections.intro: What you can rely on before any spoiler detail.
paragraphs: Official: Drag'n Wash has three endings, and each ending is about ninety minutes. That is the planning backbone for every replay.

Practical path: finish one discovery clear, keep a hub save from before late branches, then specialize comfort attention on one dragon route per replay. Community discussion commonly orients those routes around Ryan, Alexander, and Conrad.
Exact dialogue trees and trust percentage tables are not published here. Follow on-screen prompts, keep named saves, and use the table below for route focus and risk notes.

sections.heading: Spoiler Warning
sections.intro: This page discusses ending structure, route focus, and late-game save behavior.
paragraphs: If you want a completely blind first clear, stop after the Quick Answer and finish one ending on your own. The rest of the page stays free of explicit sexual detail, but it does talk about multiple endings, credits behavior, softlock risks, and which character routes players commonly chase.

sections.heading: Save-Slot Strategy That Reduces Replay Waste
paragraphs: Because each ending is near ninety minutes, one overwritten file can cost an evening. Build a simple slot map before late branches.

subsections.heading: Recommended slot layout
paragraphs: Keep one early “hub” save after you understand the wash loop but before major route locks. Keep one active slot for your current ending attempt. When a visit clearly pivots toward a specific dragon’s late arc, copy that file to a named backup before you continue.
bullets: Slot A — post-tutorial / stable hub
Slot B — active route in progress
Slot C — pre-credits or pre-branch backup
Optional Slot D — second route ready to diverge

subsections.heading: Credits and continue quirks
paragraphs: Community: using continue after finishing a slot can dump you straight into credits again. Do not rely on a finished file as your branching point. Also avoid experimental credits options such as unstuck kobold, which itch comments link to softlocks. During normal play, Unstick Kobold on the pause menu is the documented recovery tool from the official Kobold Hotfix.

sections.heading: Practical Route Focus
paragraphs: High-level route advice is stable even when dialogue lists are not. Pick the dragon whose presence you want to prioritize, keep their washes thorough, and answer their comfort prompts as they appear. Split attention across every visitor evenly if you are still on a discovery clear; specialize once you are ending hunting.

Ryan draws a lot of search interest. Conrad is often discussed with later-visit caution around request order. Alexander appears in the same cast discussions. Keep expectations soft: these are orientation notes for planning, not long-form official bios.

If a personal request appears, complete it in the prompted sequence. The Kobold Hotfix addressed a known level-8 Conrad request-order softlock, and community troubleshooting still warns that skipping ahead of the visit’s request can softlock later visits. That advice is about order and prompts.

When you specialize, say the focus out loud when you name the save file. A slot labeled “Ryan pre-late” or “Conrad pre-request” is easier to trust at midnight than a generic autosave. That tiny labeling habit is as important as any Drag'n Wash endings tip about comfort priority.

paragraphs: This plan respects the official three-ending structure. If a patch changes branch timing, prompt-following and save hygiene still work.
Players who only want one favorite route still benefit from the same Drag'n Wash endings discipline: name your slots, copy before late branches, and never treat a credits file as a flexible hub.
Keep the plan boring and repeatable. A calm Drag'n Wash endings weekend is three named backups and three focused visits, not one heroic overwrite.

sections.heading: Official vs Community Labels
paragraphs: Keep labels honest while you plan Drag'n Wash endings. Official means store-page facts: three endings, about ninety minutes each, wash/chat/request loop, adult-only framing, and full controller support on Steam categories.

Community means itch-comment troubleshooting and player route habits: Ryan, Alexander, and Conrad as common focus names; clean-bar leftovers on tails and necks; credits continue quirks; credits unstuck warnings; and Conrad request-order softlocks.

Mixing those layers is how guides overclaim. Use Official numbers for time budgets. Use Community notes for risk checklists. When a patch lands, re-check Options and pause-menu recovery first—Unstick Kobold on pause is documented in the official Kobold Hotfix—then decide whether an older softlock report still applies.
If you only need one takeaway: budget three short-novel routes, protect a hub save, and treat prompt order as part of the critical path whenever Conrad’s later visits appear.

hero.heading: Drag'n Wash Controls and Tools
hero.lead: Run the wash loop smoothly on keyboard or controller, use Options comfort toggles, scout missed dirt when the clean bar stalls, and know where Unstick Kobold lives on the pause menu.

sections.heading: Controller and Input Support
paragraphs: Steam categories list full controller support for Drag'n Wash. Most Drag'n Wash controls questions start there. That makes a pad a first-class option on Windows, macOS, and Linux builds distributed through Steam or itch, including Steam Deck Verified play per official September 15, 2026 Steam news. Connect your controller before launching if you want the game to detect it cleanly on the first visit.

Open the in-game Options or rebind screen for your build’s actual mappings, then bind wash, camera, confirm, and menu actions to whatever is comfortable for long orbits around a dragon. Static third-party key charts drift across patches.

The official Kobold Hotfix Steam news (September 13, 2026) adds Invert Look Y / invert-Y mouse options and Sprayer Reduce Motion under Options. Use those if look direction or sprayer motion comfort is fighting you during long washes.

Good Drag'n Wash controls setup is boring on purpose: reliable camera orbits, comfortable confirm/cancel, and no fighting the stick while you hunt a last dirt speck. Spend two minutes in Options before your first paid visit so you are not rebinding mid-prompt.

sections.heading: Wash Tool Loop Habits
sections.intro: Tools exist to support cleaning and comfort, not a deep crafting tree.
paragraphs: Official framing is soap-and-wash service work: you clean, chat, and tend requests as comfort grows. In practice that means selecting the appropriate wash tools as the visit presents them, covering the model systematically, and switching focus when a prompt appears.

Work in passes. First pass: large surfaces you can see head-on. Second pass: sides and underside angles. Third pass: detail areas that itch comments flag as finish blockers—tail ink, back of the neck, and other easy-to-miss patches. Tool swapping mid-pass is fine; leaving entire angles untouched is what stalls jobs.

When a personal request interrupts the wash, resolve the highlighted ask, then return to cleaning. Out-of-order request completion is a community-reported softlock pattern on later Conrad visits, so treat prompts as part of the control flow.
Keep Drag'n Wash tool swaps deliberate: finish a sector, then change tools, then resume the orbit. Random swapping is how players lose track of which flank still needs soap.

steps.heading: Lock a stable camera distance
steps.description: Pick a distance where soap coverage and dirt reads are both visible. Re-center if the model fills the frame too tightly to see edges.

steps.heading: Orbit on purpose
steps.description: Move around the dragon in consistent clockwise or counterclockwise loops so you know which sectors you already cleaned.

steps.heading: Detail-scout before forcing a finish
steps.description: If the clean bar looks done, do one more slow scout of tail, neck back, and ink before assuming a bug.

sections.heading: Clean Bar Troubleshooting
paragraphs: A full-looking clean bar that will not complete the job is the top mechanical complaint in itch comments. The usual cause is missed dirt rather than a broken meter.
If scouting fails twice, reload an earlier save and repeat with slower orbits. Combine this checklist with the beginner guide’s first-wash steps when you are still learning model silhouettes.
Most “broken meter” reports in Drag'n Wash controls threads resolve after a slower third pass. Treat the checklist as muscle memory before you file a bug or reinstall.

sections.heading: Credits Menu and Recovery Cautions
paragraphs: Controls are not only about washing. Community reports say selecting unstuck kobold during credits can softlock. After an ending, prefer known-good menu exits and rely on backup saves instead of experimental credits options.
Likewise, continuing a finished slot may throw you back into credits. That is a save-planning issue as much as a controls issue—keep pre-credits backups when you still intend to branch.

Put differently: the riskiest Drag'n Wash “button” late in a run is often a credits menu curiosity, not a wash tool. Finish, quit cleanly, and reload a named backup when you are ready for the next route.

hero.heading: Drag'n Wash VR Mod
hero.lead: Drag'n Wash does not list native VR on official store pages. A community mod on itch.io adds experimental headset play. This page covers ownership, Easy Install ZIP mindset, Steam launch flags, hotkeys, and safety checks—without hosting binaries.

sections.heading: Official Game vs Community VR
paragraphs: The shipping game on Steam and itch is a flat single-player simulation with full controller support listed on Steam. Native VR is not part of the official feature set on those store pages. Anything that puts you in a headset is third-party and may break after patches.

The community project lives at the RandomCat4 itch page for the Drag'n Wash VR mod. It is described as using BepInEx 6 beta with UnityVRMod, and it is in development. Always read the mod page’s current instructions—this guide summarizes widely repeated setup notes so you know what to verify.

You must own the game. Mods that require a legitimate Steam or itch install are not a substitute for buying Drag'n Wash. This site will not host mod files or mirrors; link through the itch project only.

Search results that imply “Drag'n Wash VR” is a built-in Steam feature are misleading. Treat headset support as optional community tooling layered onto the same adult simulation, with the usual backup and compatibility caution.

sections.heading: Pre-Install Checklist
sections.intro: Do these before touching game folders.

steps.heading: Own and launch the base game once
steps.description: Confirm a normal flat boot from Steam or itch on Windows. Finish at least one short wash so you know the save folder and Options menus.

steps.heading: Backup saves and the game directory
steps.description: Copy your save slots and consider a full game folder backup. Experimental loaders can fail mid-update.

steps.heading: Use the Easy Install ZIP from the author page
steps.description: Prefer the mod author’s Easy Install ZIP and README on itch. Confirm current BepInEx 6 beta / UnityVRMod requirements against the live game build.

steps.heading: Plan a rollback
steps.description: Know how to remove the loader and verify files on Steam if the mod breaks boot. Keep a non-VR shortcut for comparison.

sections.heading: Launch Flags and Hotkeys
paragraphs: Community setup notes repeatedly mention a Steam launch option of `%command% -force-d3d11`. That flag forces a Direct3D 11 path some Unity VR tooling expects. Set it in Steam’s launch options for the game if the mod documentation still calls for it, then remove or adjust it if the author updates guidance.

While in VR, community notes reference F10 to recenter and F11 to toggle VR. Treat those as mod hotkeys layered on top of the base game, not as official Steam control categories. If they conflict with your rebinds, check both the mod README and in-game Options.
If the mod crashes, the itch page notes a `-force-gfx-direct` tip. Try that only after you confirm ownership, backups, and the primary `-force-d3d11` guidance still match the current README.

Because the mod is in development, expect occasional breakage when Gator Dragon Games patches the base simulation. After any game update, re-read the itch page before assuming yesterday’s install still works.

table.caption: VR setup quick reference
rows: Required — buy on Steam or itch

sections.heading: Safety, Comfort, and SFW Notes
paragraphs: Wash simulations involve close camera work. In VR, start with short sessions, keep recenter handy, and stop if motion comfort drops. Flat Options such as Invert Look Y and Sprayer Reduce Motion still matter as a baseline before you add headset complexity.
The base game is adult-only. VR does not change the content rating—it only changes presentation. This site remains SFW: we discuss install safety and controls, not explicit scenes.
Never install loaders from random reupload mirrors. Prefer the mod author’s itch page, keep antivirus realism in mind with injected runtimes, and do not share cracked copies.

A safe Drag'n Wash VR experiment is one you can undo in five minutes: backups ready, author README open, flat shortcut still working, and no irreplaceable ending save left only inside a modded directory.

sections.heading: When Not to Use VR Yet
paragraphs: Skip the mod until you can finish washes cleanly in flat mode. Debugging a missed dirt spot is harder when you are also debugging a loader. If you are mid-ending hunt with precious saves, finish those routes before experimenting.
Also wait if a fresh game patch just dropped and the mod page has not confirmed compatibility. Official three-ending progress is easier to protect with a stable flat install.

If you came here only to learn whether headset support is official, you already have the answer: it is not listed on the store pages. Bookmark the community Drag'n Wash VR mod page for later, then return to flat guides until your saves and comfort settings are steady.

sections.heading: VR Boot Troubleshooting Mindset
sections.intro: When headset play fails, isolate layers instead of reinstalling everything at once.
paragraphs: A broken Drag'n Wash VR mod boot is usually one of four layers: base game update mismatch, loader install drift, launch-option mismatch, or headset runtime not ready. Change one layer at a time and keep the flat shortcut as your control test.

If the flat game still launches, your saves and ownership are fine—focus on the mod README, `%command% -force-d3d11` if still required, then `-force-gfx-direct` only if crashes persist, and whether F10/F11 even load. If flat boot also fails after folder edits, verify Steam files or restore the backed-up game directory before touching the headset stack again.

subsections.heading: Quick isolation order
paragraphs: Work top-down so you do not chase headset drivers for a missing BepInEx file.
bullets: Confirm flat boot with a non-VR shortcut
Re-read the itch README for the current game build
Check the Steam launch option against current docs
Try the documented crash tip only after the primary flag
Only then test recenter/toggle hotkeys in a short session

faq.answer: No native VR is listed on official Steam or itch store pages. Headset play currently means a community mod.

title: How to Escape Drag'n Wash: Unstick & Softlocks
description: Escape stuck states in Drag'n Wash: Unstick Kobold, clean-bar leftovers, Conrad request-order softlocks, geometry traps, and when to reload a save.
searchIntent: Players stuck in geometry, clean-bar finishes, or softlocks who need recovery steps.

hero.heading: How to Escape Drag'n Wash
hero.lead: Use this checklist when Drag'n Wash leaves you stuck in geometry, a clean bar that will not finish, a Conrad request-order softlock, or a bad credits menu choice. Start with pause-menu Unstick Kobold, then escalate to scouting, prompt order, and save reloads.

sections.heading: Quick Answer Checklist
sections.intro: Most stuck Drag'n Wash reports resolve with one of these four paths.
paragraphs: Work top-down through this How to Escape Drag'n Wash checklist. Do not jump straight to deleting saves if pause-menu recovery or a missed dirt spot can fix the visit.

table.caption: Stuck state → first fix
rows: Clipped / cannot move in a visit
Clean bar looks done, job blocked
Restart job, then reload earlier save
Late Conrad visit frozen after requests

subsections.heading: Four recovery paths
paragraphs: Most stuck reports resolve with one of these four paths.
bullets: Geometry stuck during play → open pause menu → Unstick Kobold
Clean bar full but job will not end → restart/re-scout tail ink and neck; missed dirt is the usual itch-comment cause
Conrad later visit softlock feel → reload a pre-request save; complete personal requests in the prompted order
Credits menu experiments → avoid unstuck kobold during credits; reload a pre-credits backup if softlocked

sections.heading: Unstick Kobold on the Pause Menu
paragraphs: Official Kobold Hotfix Steam news (September 13, 2026) documents Unstick Kobold on the game/pause menu. That is the intended recovery tool when you are stuck during play—wedged in geometry, unable to re-center usefully, or otherwise trapped mid-visit.

Open pause, choose Unstick Kobold, then confirm you can move and resume washing or chatting. If the tool frees you, save to a new slot before continuing a valuable route so you are not one misclick away from the same trap.

Community warning still matters: itch comments say selecting unstuck kobold during credits can softlock. Pause-menu Unstick Kobold during visits is not the same as experimenting in the credits UI. Keep those contexts separate.
If Unstick Kobold frees you during a valuable Drag'n Wash route, copy the slot immediately. Recovery without a backup only solves the current clip, not the next one.

steps.heading: Pause immediately
steps.description: Do not mash random movement for minutes. Open the pause menu as soon as you confirm you cannot progress.

steps.heading: Select Unstick Kobold
steps.description: Use the pause-menu recovery option documented in the official Kobold Hotfix Steam news.

steps.heading: Reorient and save
steps.description: Check camera and movement, finish the current safe action, then write a fresh backup if this route matters.

sections.heading: Clean Bar Full but Job Will Not End
paragraphs: This is not always a Drag'n Wash softlock. Itch comments repeatedly describe a clean bar that looks complete while leftover dirt remains—especially ink on a tail or spots on the back of the neck. The job finish state waits on those patches.

Change camera height, orbit both flanks, and deliberately scrub patterned or inked areas. Restart the job if the game allows a fresh pass. Only after two careful scouts should you treat the state as something that needs a reload.

subsections.heading: Scout order that usually works
paragraphs: Use the same scavenger pass every time so you keep a consistent search pattern under stress.
bullets: Front and large surfaces
Left and right flanks
Tail including ink
Back of the neck
Underside / hard camera angles last

sections.heading: Conrad Request-Order Softlock
paragraphs: The official Kobold Hotfix addresses a Conrad softlock for a known level-8 request-order case. Community itch comments still describe later-visit softlock risk when personal requests are completed out of the prompted order—for example, skipping ahead of the visit’s request. Keep the advice SFW and mechanical.

Complete personal requests in the prompted order. Do not skip ahead of the visit’s request. Even after the hotfix, treat prompt order as the safe path. If you already skipped ahead and the visit no longer advances, reload a save from before that request chain.
If you do not have a pre-request backup, you may need to replay more of the visit. That is painful, which is why Conrad-focused runs deserve a named save before late personal request sequences.
Players hunting multiple Drag'n Wash endings should treat Conrad’s later visits as high-risk save points even on non-Conrad routes. A shared early file can still brick if request order breaks.

sections.heading: Geometry Stuck and When to Reload
paragraphs: Geometry stuck usually means your avatar or camera is clipped somewhere the wash tools cannot usefully reach. Try Unstick Kobold first. If you remain stuck after one or two pause-menu recoveries, reload.

Reload when: Unstick Kobold fails twice; a clean-bar scout fails twice after a job restart; a Conrad visit no longer responds after out-of-order requests; or credits menu experimentation softlocked the file.

Do not keep hammering a credits softlock hoping for a hidden exit. Force-quit if the UI is dead, then load the pre-credits backup. Continuing a finished slot can also dump you back into credits—another reason finished files make poor hubs.
Write the stuck class into your Drag'n Wash save note when you reload: geometry, clean-bar, request-order, or credits. That label stops you from repeating the same failed fix five minutes later.

steps.heading: Identify the stuck class
steps.description: Geometry, clean-bar leftovers, request-order softlock, or credits menu.

steps.heading: Apply the matching first fix
steps.description: Unstick Kobold, re-scout dirt, honor prompt order via reload, or abandon credits experiments.

steps.heading: Escalate to an earlier save
steps.description: Pick the newest save that still predates the bad state. Label a new slot after recovery.

steps.heading: Prevent the repeat
steps.description: For routes you care about, keep hub + active + pre-late backups as described in the endings guide.

sections.heading: Prevention Habits
paragraphs: Most How to Escape Drag'n Wash searches are preventable with three habits: scout tails and necks before blaming the meter, honor personal request order, and never make the credits screen your sandbox. Those habits keep Drag'n Wash evenings short and recoverable.

Also turn on comfort Options if camera or sprayer motion is making you miss dirt: Invert Look Y and Sprayer Reduce Motion are documented in the same official Kobold Hotfix that added pause-menu Unstick Kobold.
If you are mid-ending hunt, postpone community VR experiments until your flat saves are safe. Headset debugging on top of a softlock is how evenings disappear.

faq.question: Where is Unstick Kobold?
faq.answer: On the pause / game menu per the official Kobold Hotfix Steam news. Use it during play when you are stuck, not as a credits experiment.

faq.question: Why is my clean bar full but the job unfinished?
faq.answer: Itch comments usually blame missed dirt such as tail ink or the back of the neck. Restart and re-scout before assuming a softlock.

faq.question: How do I avoid the Conrad softlock?
faq.answer: The Kobold Hotfix addressed a known level-8 Conrad request-order softlock. Still complete personal requests in the prompted order, do not skip ahead of the visit’s request, and keep a save before late Conrad request chains.

faq.question: When should I reload instead of unsticking?
faq.answer: If Unstick Kobold fails twice, if dirt scouting fails twice, if a request-order softlock already happened, or if credits menu choices froze the file.

faq.question: Can continue after an ending get me stuck in credits?
faq.answer: Players report that continuing a finished slot can dump you back into credits. Branch from a pre-credits backup instead.
